text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

- Authorities have spent 97 million crowns in the last two years on sending foreigners without residency permits back to their home countries. Anders Sjaastad, a member of parliament's justice committee, says the costs are higher than expected, which indicates bad organisation.
- Despite higher freight rates in the shipping market, many shipowners are concerned that the large amount of tanker tonnage on order could harm the market in a few years.

- Environmental groups Bellona and Norges Naturvern Forbund say that granting Naturkraft a concession to build two natural gas power plants could be in conflict with the law. The organisations say the government can grant permission to build the plants, but not to increase discharges of carbon dioxide.

- A subsidiary of the state-owned telecommunications company Telenor, Telenor Venture, is investing heavily in the United States. In past week the company has spend eight million crowns buying shares in American companies.
